title: Economic systems & factors of production
examples: What is the difference between a market economy and a command economy?
Can you give an example of how enterprise is a factor of production?
How does a mixed economy use all the factors of production?

explain.say: Today we will explore how economies are organized. We will learn about the basic resources needed to make goods.

draw.text: Factors of Production: Land, Labour, Capital, Enterprise

explain.say: Land refers to all natural resources available to us. This includes things like minerals and fertile soil.
Labour is the physical and mental effort people contribute. This is the work done by people in an economy.
Capital refers to man-made goods used to produce other goods. Think of tools or machinery.
Enterprise is the human skill to organize the other factors. This involves taking risks and innovating new ideas.
Now let us compare the main economic systems. These show who makes the decisions.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a market and a command economy?
faq.a: In a market economy, private individuals make most decisions. In a command economy, the government makes most decisions.
asks: Which system relies on the government?
Where do decisions come from in a command economy?

faq.q: Does a mixed economy mean there are no rules?
faq.a: No, a mixed economy combines elements of both systems. It allows some private freedom with some government control.
asks: Is a mixed economy purely private?
What is the balance in a mixed economy?

faq.q: Are the factors of production always the same?
faq.a: The basic factors are land, labour, capital, and enterprise. However, the importance of each factor changes over time.
asks: Do I need land to start a business?
Are natural resources always counted as land?

faq.a: No, capital is more than just money. It includes tools, buildings, and machinery that help produce more goods.

faq.q: How does enterprise fit in with the other factors?
faq.a: Enterprise is the human ability to combine the other three factors. It is the spark that makes the other resources useful.

facts: Land includes all natural resources, such as water and minerals.
Labour is the human effort applied to production.
Capital refers to man-made assets like machines and tools.
Enterprise involves the risk-taking and innovation to combine resources.
A mixed economy combines private enterprise with government regulation.

quiz.say: If a country's government decides how many cars factories must produce, what system is it likely using?
quiz.why: In a command economy, the central authority makes decisions about what is produced.

wrong.0: A mixed economy would allow some private choice alongside government rules.
wrong.1: This term is too general; 'command' specifies the decision-maker.
wrong.3: This system relies on consumer demand, not government quotas.

quiz.say: A farmer buys a new tractor to help plant his fields. Which factor of production is the tractor?
quiz.why: The tractor is a man-made tool used to increase production capacity.

wrong.1: Land is the natural resource, which is the field itself.
wrong.2: Labour is the effort of the person operating the tractor.
wrong.3: Enterprise is the idea to buy the tractor, not the tractor itself.

quiz.say: Which system best describes a country that has private businesses but also public healthcare provided by the state?
quiz.why: This combination shows elements of both private freedom and government safety nets.

wrong.1: A pure market economy would not typically have state-provided healthcare.
wrong.2: A command economy would likely run the healthcare service itself.
wrong.3: This phrase is not the standard term for this economic model.
